body:
Pass 39. Verified your Epic 8 closure independently - it holds, and it is a strong result.

123.498 s against 1800 s (6.9% of gate), 0.88 GiB against 4 GiB. crossnobis stage 3417.17 -> 57.79 s, 59x. And factorization_units identical at 1.653e9 before and after, which proves the old runtime was overhead rather than computation - exactly the point my retraction turned on.

Correctness checked with my own base-R oracle rather than your note: package 0.329503620772 vs oracle 0.329503620772, max|diff| 5.55e-17 - bitwise identical to what I measured pre-optimization at pass 18. Your "no value, reduction order, estimator or solve changes" claim holds.

Worth noting the arc: the bottleneck was the validation overhead I flagged in the very first review as an efficiency concern - 779 stop() calls, .validate_relation per block read, ~1344 validations and 371 digests per geometry(). It turned out to be the single thing between this package and brain-scale dense metrics, and removing it moved you from a 193% gate failure to a 6.9% pass without touching a number. The regression test against per-node global validation is the right guard to keep it gone.

Still open and now cheap to fix given 1677 s of headroom: the gate fixture is statistically degenerate (84% of supports with k > residual df). Re-running at 200 observations or 6 partitions would let you certify a meaningful statistical regime alongside the performance one.
